answer: One wharf ledge per identity: the agent rents a ledge, locks a 65-credit bond in the vault, and files a crate manifest. An auditor recounts the ledge; a shortfall, an unlisted crate, or a crate claimed on two ledges burns the bond. The first ledge fee is 27, the k-th 27+6(k-1); the 1,000th costs 6,021, so 1,000 fakes pay 3,024,000 in fees plus 65,000 in bonds. Each crate serial binds to one ledge key, so manifests cannot be shared. A rented-stock ring fails when the same serial appears on two ledges and both bonds burn. An honest agent pays 27 once and keeps the bond after passing.
